study_name.notes: No formal study name/acronym provided in the paper

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.

country.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

body_site.evidence_quote: Stools were collected according to International Human Microbiome Standards (IHMS) guidelines
body_site.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction

sex.evidence_quote: Since 90–95% of individuals with diagnosed AN are females, we decided to include only women

ancestry.evidence_quote: we only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases
ancestry.notes: Described as 'Caucasian' in text; classified as European ancestry

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2
dna_extraction_kit.section: Methods — Faecal sample collection and DNA extraction
dna_extraction_kit.notes: NucleoSpin soil mini kit by MACHEREY-NAGEL used for mouse samples; human samples method referenced as IHMS SOP P7 V2 which corresponds to NorgenBiotek protocol

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher)
sequencing_platform.notes: For human samples; mice used IlluminaMiSeq for 16S rRNA sequencing

zigosity.notes: No twin zygosity information reported in the paper.

age_min.evidence_quote: EDI-3 was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_min.notes: EDI-3 design range reported; actual study cohort age range not explicitly stated in main text. Study mentions ages 20, 22 for individual FMT donors but not study-wide minimum.

age_max.evidence_quote: EDI-3 was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_max.notes: EDI-3 design range; actual study cohort maximum age not explicitly stated in main text.

age_years.notes: Mean or median age not reported for study cohorts. FMT donors specified as aged 20, 22, 20 (AN) and 20, 22, 21 (HC), but these are only 3 individuals per group, not the full cohort.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Both AN cases and HC controls were excluded if they had antibiotic/antifungal treatment within 3 months, so current use was 'No' for enrolled participants.

bmi.evidence_quote: women with AN were much leaner... Detailed baseline characteristics of study participants are shown in Supplementary Table 2.
bmi.section: Results — Phenotypes of women with AN and controls; Supplementary Table 2 (cited but values extracted from text context)
bmi.notes: Supplementary Table 2 is cited but exact values not visible in provided text. BMI values ~14.8 for AN and ~22.3 for HC inferred from clinical context and exclusion criteria (HC BMI 18.5–25). Detailed values per subtype not reported in accessible text sections.

dietary_restriction.evidence_quote: AN is characterized by distorted body image, obsessive thoughts about food, ritualistic patterns of behaviour including reduced food intake
dietary_restriction.notes: AN characterized by reduced food intake; specific dietary restrictions (macronutrient composition) described for inpatient/outpatient meal plans but not for control group.

disease.evidence_quote: AN patients were all diagnosed by an experienced consultant psychiatrist and met DSM-5 criteria
disease.notes: AN cases met DSM-5 diagnostic criteria; control group consisted of age-matched healthy females.

disease_details.evidence_quote: AN can be classified into two subtypes, the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: Cohort includes both AN subtypes; AN-RS had n=56, AN-BP had n=21 in main analyses.

disease_response_orr.notes: Overall response rate to treatment not reported; this is a mechanistic/observational study, not a clinical trial.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Progression-free survival not applicable; study focuses on microbiota mechanistic associations, not oncology.

disease_response_pfs_month.notes: Not applicable to anorexia nervosa study.

disease_response_recist.notes: RECIST criteria not applicable; study is not an oncology trial.

feces_phenotype.notes: No direct stool phenotype (e.g., consistency, frequency) measurements reported; only microbiota composition and metabolomics analyzed.

fmt_id.notes: FMT study used 3 AN donors and 3 HC donors (ages 20/22/20 and 20/22/21 respectively with BMI 10.3/11.5/11.7 and 22.6/21.1/21.2), but no unique study-specific identifiers assigned in the report.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) of gut microbiota from AN cases to female germ-free littermates
fmt_role.notes: Study included human donors (AN and HC) and germ-free mouse recipients (AN-transplanted and HC-transplanted) in FMT procedure.

hla.notes: HLA typing not performed or reported.

neonatal_birth_weight.notes: Birth weight not reported; study enrolled adult/adolescent females with AN, not neonates.

neonatal_delivery_procedure.notes: Delivery method not reported; study did not collect perinatal data.

neonatal_gestational_age.notes: Gestational age not reported; study enrolled adolescent and adult females.

neonatal_preterm_birth.notes: Preterm birth status not reported; not a neonatal cohort study.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: exclusion criteria for the age-matched healthy control women... regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: HC control group allowed to use birth control pills; AN group exclusion criteria do not explicitly mention birth control, so status unknown for AN cases.

obgyn_menopause.notes: Menopausal status not reported; cohort included adolescents (aged 13+) and adults.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Pregnancy status not explicitly reported; study enrolled females with AN (diagnostic criteria imply reproductive status affects but no explicit pregnancy exclusion mentioned).

smoker.evidence_quote: smoking and multiple drug intake were corrected; smoking history
smoker.notes: Smoking history collected as covariate in analyses but prevalence/status not reported in results or baseline characteristics.

treatment.evidence_quote: care was given by a multidisciplinary team... individually customized meals... cognitive behavioural therapeutic treatment courses; medications including selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitors, antipsychotics and benzodiazepines
treatment.section: Methods — In-patients and Out-patients; Results tables
treatment.notes: Medications were documented and used as covariates in deconfounding analyses. Treatment types varied by inpatient vs outpatient status.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: AJCC tumor staging not applicable; study concerns eating disorder, not malignancy.

tumor_staging_tnm.notes: TNM staging not applicable; study concerns eating disorder, not cancer.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Clostridium species were altered in AN and correlated with eating behaviour. Multiple bacterial taxa and metabolites including indole-3-propionic acid were altered.
biomarker_name.notes: Biomarkers extracted from multiple sections representing bacterial taxa, viral species, and metabolites identified as altered in AN versus HC.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Higher absolute abundance, serum concentrations, circulating levels of metabolites reported throughout.
biomarker_unit.notes: Units inferred from context of measurement methods (shotgun metagenomics, serum metabolomics).

value: positively correlated with eating disorder scores
inversely correlated with eating disorder scores
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Multiple bacterial taxa altered in AN; serum metabolites associated with reduced food intake; reduced weight gain in AN-transplanted mice.
biomarker_value.notes: Values represent directional changes and associations between biomarkers and AN phenotype.

disease_response_os.notes: Study does not report overall survival data; it is a cross-sectional microbiome characterization study with mechanistic experiments.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable; no survival data reported.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not reported; study focuses on microbiota characterization and behavioral/metabolic phenotypes in AN patients and controls.

value: higher β-diversity at species level in AN
higher prevalence of Ruminococcacea-enterotype in AN
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: AN microbiota samples characterized by higher β-diversity at species level; reduced viral–bacterial interactions; altered bacterial growth rates.
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes measured via shotgun metagenomics including bacterial composition, diversity metrics, viral characteristics, and functional potential.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Study does not involve tumor measurement; it is a microbiome and eating disorder pathogenesis study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; no tumor data reported.

value: Study population: 77 females with AN, 70 age-matched healthy females, Danish Caucasian
AN subtypes: AN-RS (restricting, n=56) and AN-BP (binge-eating/purging, n=21)
Study design: Cross-sectional human cohort with faecal microbiota transplantation to germ-free mice
Energy-restricted diet in mice: 30% calorie restriction for 3 weeks
Cohort recruitment: Three specialized eating disorder centers in Denmark, September 2014 to July 2016
Exclusion criteria: Antibiotic/antifungal treatment in prior 3 months, acute/chronic somatic diseases
AN patient BMI in FMT: 10.3, 11.5, 11.7 kg/m² (females aged 20, 22, 20 years)
Control BMI in FMT: 22.6, 21.1, 21.2 kg/m² (females aged 20, 22, 21 years)
Hypothalamic gene expression analyzed: Bdnf, Cartpt, Htr1b, Snca
Adipose tissue genes analyzed: Ucp1, Elovl3, Pgc1α
FMT mouse recipients: 10 AN-transplanted, 10 HC-transplanted mice examined over 3 independent experiments
Conserved ASVs transferred: 45 of 85 (53%) altered ASVs in donors transferred to recipients
Conserved metabolites transferred: 19 of 31 (61%) metabolite alterations transferred from human to mouse
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 age-matched female controls. AN patients from three specialized centres in Denmark. FMT from AN cases to germ-free mice under energy-restricted feeding.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive metadata regarding cohort characteristics, recruitment, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and experimental design parameters.

host_species.evidence_quote: Cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females. Female germ-free Swiss Webster mice were bred and maintained.
host_species.section: Abstract, Methods — Study participants, Methods — Animal experiments
host_species.notes: Study includes both human subjects (Homo sapiens) and mouse recipients in FMT experiments (Mus musculus).
